title: A prokaryotic cell
caption: A bacterium has no nucleus: its single circular chromosome lies in the nucleoid, free in the cytoplasm. Plasmids, 70S ribosomes, a wall, and often a capsule, pili and a flagellum complete the cell, typically 0.5–5 µm long.
alt: A rod-shaped bacterium with labels for the capsule, cell wall, plasma membrane, cytoplasm, nucleoid, plasmid, 70S ribosomes, pili and a flagellum.
description: The capsule is the outer slimy layer; inside it is the cell wall, then the plasma membrane.
The nucleoid holds the single, usually circular chromosome, with no membrane around it.
Plasmids are small extra circles of DNA, often carrying genes such as antibiotic resistance.
70S ribosomes are scattered through the cytoplasm.
Pili on the surface attach the cell and transfer DNA; the flagellum turns to move it.
There is no nucleus, and no mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum or Golgi apparatus.
